answer: No—not by itself. A recorded supervision event or completed reconciliation may evidence an activity, but does not establish that supervision was adequate or ownership records were proper. That conclusion requires an applicable legal standard and reliable facts showing that the activity met it across the relevant scope and period. The retained provisions provide qualitative requirements, not a rule that one recorded event establishes fulfillment.

claims.inference: The text distinguishes ongoing supervision and periodic review from the mere occurrence of an event. Applying it requires assessing the quality, coverage and continuity of monitoring. UT 6.11C concerns outsourced valuation; transferring it to other tokenisation activities needs a separate legal justification.
missing_premises: The UT provision applies to this scheme, management company, outsourced valuation activity and assessment period, subject to applicable conditions or relaxations.
An applicable interpretation of reasonable care, skill and diligence, ongoing supervision and periodic review.
Reliable evidence of what was reviewed, by whom, with what competence and resources, how frequently, what deficiencies were found and how they were addressed.
claims.proposition: A recorded supervision event alone does not establish fulfillment of UT 6.11C.

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party in ensuring such entity possesses the appropriate level of knowledge, experience and resources that commensurate with the appropriate valuation policies and procedures for each scheme.
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.

claims.inference: Reconciliation is identified as a consideration, not a sufficient compliance test. Completion does not establish that the inputs reflected legally valid interests, all relevant records were covered, or discrepancies were resolved. These are proposed evidential inquiries, not an exhaustive checklist expressly prescribed by the source.
missing_premises: Applicability of paragraph 11 and the Appendix factors to the product, actor and period.
The governing ownership rights, settlement-finality rules and authoritative records against which correctness is assessed.
An applicable standard for proper records and suitable reconciliation coverage and frequency.
Evidence of input accuracy and completeness, relevant holders and transactions covered, reconciliation results, unresolved discrepancies and corrective action.
Evidence that the arrangement is operationally compatible with involved service providers.
claims.proposition: A completed reconciliation alone does not establish proper ownership records under paragraph 11.
claims.status: Source-supported deduction; adequacy assessment requires additional premises

support.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

For example, whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

claims.inference: The text preserves responsibility despite outsourcing. Allocation of authority, actual supervisory conduct and operational or record-keeping outcomes are distinct evidential questions. Neither contractual retention of responsibility nor a logged activity supplies a complete discharge test.
missing_premises: The assessed entity is the relevant Product Provider and the retained edition applies throughout the assessment interval.
A justified interpretation of what fulfills the responsibility requirement in the particular arrangement.
Evidence of retained authority, information access and capacity to intervene, actual oversight, and operational and record-keeping performance.
claims.proposition: Retained responsibility under paragraph 10 is not proved fulfilled merely by showing that a provider or delegate performed an activity.
claims.status: Textual responsibility rule plus deduction; sufficiency standard unresolved

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: A register-maintenance duty attaches to specified roles; Product Provider status alone does not establish that role. Modal words must also be understood within the Code's regulatory status and applicable authorisation conditions, rather than treated as freestanding statutory duties.
missing_premises: Identification of the scheme, trustee or appointed register keeper.
Applicable authorisation conditions, amendments and any modification or relaxation.
Evidence that the register actually maintained accurately reflects the relevant holders and interests over the assessed period.
claims.proposition: Any reliance on UT 6.8 requires role-specific applicability and evidence of register maintenance, not merely a reconciliation record.

support.quote: The scheme, or in the case of a unit trust, the trustee or the person so appointed by the trustee must maintain a register of holders.
This UT Code does not have the force of law.

The Commission may modify or relax the application of a requirement in this UT Code if it considers that, in particular circumstances, strict application of the requirement would operate in an unduly burdensome or unnecessarily restrictive manner.

rival_readings: Paragraph 10 may primarily allocate continuing ultimate responsibility; alternatively, its references to management, operational soundness and record keeping may support a substantive conduct-and-performance assessment. The retained wording does not supply a complete fulfillment test for either reading.

A supervision or reconciliation record may contribute materially to fulfillment when its contents and surrounding evidence demonstrate the applicable standard. Treating the bare occurrence or completion flag as sufficient has no support in the quoted provisions.
unresolved: No actual supervision records, reconciliation results, governing product documents or applicable authorisation conditions are supplied.
The precise adequacy standard, assessment period and evidential sufficiency remain unresolved; absence of proof of fulfillment does not itself establish breach.
The supplied computational acceptance and round-trip results do not establish legal applicability, the truth of factual premises or fulfillment.
